item.title: Hits That Have Topped Both the Billboard Hot 100 & Hot Country Songs Charts
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the fascinating world of music. Today, we're celebrating a milestone in country music history. On October 20, 1958, Billboard introduced the Hot Country Songs chart, which has since become the genre's main songs survey.
[Short music transition]
Host: But that's not all - just two months earlier, on August 4, 1958, the all-genre Billboard Hot 100 was launched. The country chart built upon the Hot 100's momentum, providing the fastest and most accurate coverage of country music records. And it wasn't long before we saw songs topping both charts.
[Short music transition]
Host: The first song to achieve this feat was Johnny Horton's "The Battle of New Orleans", which hit number one on the Hot Country Songs chart on May 18, 1959, and then led the Hot 100 two weeks later. Since then, 32 songs have crowned both charts, showcasing the most elite crossover dominance between genres.
[Short music transition]
Host: The 2020s have seen the most songs achieve this crossover success, with 12 titles reaching number one on both charts. And some artists have stood out for their ability to dominate both charts. Morgan Wallen leads the pack with four shared number one hits, followed by Taylor Swift with three.
[Short music transition]
Host: Other notable artists, such as Glen Campbell, John Denver, Dolly Parton, and Kenny Rogers, have each achieved two number one hits on both charts. These songs have become a staple of music history, and we're excited to share them with you.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for joining us on this journey through country music history. Join us next time as we explore more fascinating stories and facts from the world of music.
